thread:
Liam (IC): Hey team, quick clarification on blackout rules. I have a planned medical appointment on Dec 23 that I can't move. Is Dec 23 considered a blackout day?

PeopleOps Bot: Reminder: current company-wide holiday blackout is Dec 20-27. Time off in that window requires manager approval plus People Ops sign-off per PTO policy 3.2.

Liam (IC): Got it. I read the policy but couldn't tell if medical exceptions are treated differently from vacation.

Tasha (People Ops): Short answer: medical appointments are eligible for exception but we still need manager attestation and a coverage plan if you are on any critical rotation. If it's a short partial-day appointment, managers can approve and People Ops typically rubber-stamps once coverage is verified.

Ravi (Manager): Liam, what hours are you out for on the 23rd? Any oncall overlap?

Liam (IC): Appointment 10:00-13:00 PST. No oncall shift that day. I'm on a feature sprint but can hand off any blockers.

Ravi (Manager): OK. No oncall risk. I can approve manager-side and note that Sasha will triage any production pings.

Sasha (PM): I'll be available that morning and can escalate if anything shows up.

Tasha (People Ops): Great. Liam, submit the TimeOff request and pick "Blackout Exception - Medical" and attach Ravi's approval note. We will not require unpaid marking for medical exceptions unless accrual is zero and you request unpaid.

Liam (IC): My accrual shows 2.5 hours left for the year. Will that be deducted first?

Payroll Bot: Accruals are consumed in this order: current year balance, carryover, then unpaid. If you have partial hours, People Ops flags medical exceptions to avoid year-end carryover miscounts.

Olga (Comp): For auditing: mark the request as "med-exception" in the TimeOff app so HR can separate policy-based exceptions from discretionary approvals.

Tasha (People Ops): Filing note: policy reference PTO-3.2.a (medical exceptions), temp exception ID MED-2026-07. Expect People Ops sign-off within 24 hours for medical exceptions with manager attestation.

Liam (IC): Submitted request ID 20270311 with Ravi's note and Sasha tagged. Thanks team.

PeopleOps Bot: Request 20270311 queued for review.

Tasha (People Ops): Approved. Marked as "Medical Exception - Approved". No unpaid portion required. Closing loop.

Liam (IC): Appreciate it. I'll update the calendar invite and leave a quick handover in the sprint channel.
